You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

== task_c3ae2279_block_overlap_rule
ARC task-c3ae2279 (solved, 2 demos): grid split by a full separator line/col of uniform color (e.g. 7/9/3) into two blocks. OUTPUT dims = block dims; cell = 2 where BOTH blocks have a nonzero (marker) cell at that position, else 0. Not a full recolor of one block (first guess was wrong pattern); also not one-block-marker masked by other marker only where other is rare — it is simply both-nonzero overlap.

== task_c3ae2279_and_overlap_rule
ARC task-c3ae2279 SOLVED (correct after 4 wrong): grid split by a full separator line (row or col of one uniform color) into TWO regions, each = background 0 + one noise color. Output = dims of one region; cell = 2 iff that cell is NONZERO IN BOTH regions (intersection/AND of the two noise masks); else 0. Separator dropped. Decoy rules that failed: 'keep the chosen/sparser/denser region recolored to 2' — demo4 (top region 68 sevens but output only 18 twos) exposed the AND-overlap rule. Lesson: when every region-selection rule fits demos but fails the test, check operations BETWEEN the two regions (AND/OR/XOR), not selection.

== task_c3ae2279_region_intersection
ARC task-c3ae2279 SOLVED (2 demos, 0 wrong): grid split into two regions by a full divider line/row of a uniform color (e.g. 9s row, or 3s column). Rule: output grid (same shape as one region) has 2 where BOTH regions have a non-zero cell at the corresponding relative position, 0 elsewhere. Output color always 2. Verify alignment by matching region dims.

== task_c3ae2279_mask_rule
ARC task-c3ae2279 SOLVED (validated correct): grid split by a full vertical separator line (color 1 in test, 4 in demo) into left region (scattered 8s on 0 background) and right region (uniform 5/6 with 0 holes), both same width. Rule: output has same dims as left region; cell = 2 where left cell is 8 AND aligned right cell is NOT a hole (0); else 0. I.e. right-side holes mask out left 8s.

== task_c3ae2279_region_overlap
ARC task-c3ae2279 SOLVED (2 wrong, then correct): grid split by a full separator line into two same-size regions. Output = region-sized grid with marker color at cells where BOTH regions are nonzero, 0 elsewhere. Marker color is the CONSTANT 2 in every demo/test (not 'smallest missing color' — that guess cost 1 wrong). Demo 1 had a uniform second region, which made it look like 'pattern recolored'; request a demo with a non-uniform second region before assuming recolor rules.

== task_c3ae2279_bg_intersect
ARC task-c3ae2279 SOLVED (2 demos, 0 wrong): grid split by a full separator line (single row/col of one color) into region A and region B, each a binary image with its own bg/mark colors. Output = region-size grid, cell=2 where BOTH cells are background (unmarked), else 0. Demo1: L bg=1, R 0/1 -> 2 where L==1 and R==1. Demo2: bg 3 vs 7 -> 2 where both bg.
